summary: UX improvement testing for 'Neue Analyse starten' button - CRITICAL BUGS FOUND. The button does NOT directly start analysis with current symptoms. Instead, it shows 'Analyse starten' button (old behavior). Additionally, edge case validation fails - clicking with no symptoms clears saved analysis instead of showing alert.

critical.issue: 'Neue Analyse starten' does NOT directly start analysis. After clicking, it shows 'Analyse starten' button instead of loading state and direct navigation to results.
critical.expected_behavior: Should DIRECTLY start analysis with entered symptoms (show loading state → navigate to /results)
critical.actual_behavior: Clears saved state, shows 'Analyse starten' button. User must click again to start analysis. Textarea value becomes empty.
critical.root_cause: The onNewAnalysis handler calls setHasSaved(false) BEFORE analyzeSymptoms(). This causes re-render which unmounts SavedAnalysisButtons and shows AnalyzeButton. The analyzeSymptoms() call may be running with stale closure or the re-render interrupts it.
reproduction_steps: 5. Observe: 'Analyse starten' button appears, textarea becomes empty, no loading state

critical.issue: Edge case: When clicking 'Neue Analyse starten' with NO symptoms entered, it should show alert and NOT clear saved analysis. But it DOES clear saved analysis.
critical.expected_behavior: Show alert 'Bitte beschreiben Sie Ihre Symptome...' and keep two buttons visible
critical.actual_behavior: No alert shown (Alert.alert may not work on web), saved analysis cleared, 'Analyse starten' button appears
critical.root_cause: Alert.alert() from React Native may not properly block on web. The validation check should work but the condition may be evaluating incorrectly.
reproduction_steps: 5. Observe: Two buttons disappear, 'Analyse starten' appears instead of alert

Consider: 1) Call analyzeSymptoms() first and only set state after API call completes, OR 2) Keep hasSaved=true and let analyzeSymptoms handle navigation without state change during loading
FIX (HIGH): Fix Alert.alert() for web - either use a web-compatible alert library or implement a custom modal for the validation error message
VERIFY: Ensure symptomText state value is correctly captured in the callback closure when 'Neue Analyse starten' is clicked
critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx lines 160-173: The sequence clearCurrentAnalysis() → setHasSaved(false) → analyzeSymptoms() is problematic. setHasSaved(false) causes re-render which may interrupt analyzeSymptoms()
The validation (line 161) checks symptomText and selectedTags but Alert.alert() may not block execution on web platform
Consider using isLoading state to prevent UI changes until API call completes

context_for_next_testing_agent: UX improvement for 'Neue Analyse starten' button is NOT working correctly. Main issues: 1) Button resets to 'Analyse starten' instead of directly starting analysis, 2) Edge case validation (no symptoms) fails to show alert and incorrectly clears saved analysis. The root cause is likely the state update sequence in onNewAnalysis handler - setHasSaved(false) triggers re-render before analyzeSymptoms() can complete.

suggested_fix.approach: Modify onNewAnalysis to call analyzeSymptoms() directly without clearing hasSaved state first. The analyzeSymptoms function will handle setting hasSaved=true and navigation on success.
suggested_fix.code_change: Replace lines 170-172 with just: analyzeSymptoms(); - let the success handler in analyzeSymptoms manage the state

rca_of_issue.root_cause: Race condition between state update and async function call. When setHasSaved(false) is called, React re-renders the component which unmounts SavedAnalysisButtons. The analyzeSymptoms() function may be running but the UI has already changed. Additionally, the textarea value appears to be cleared during re-render.
rca_of_issue.mitigation: Do not modify hasSaved state in onNewAnalysis. Let analyzeSymptoms() run and it will set hasSaved=true on success. Alternatively, show loading state while keeping two buttons, then update UI only on success/failure.
